phase2_status_history.note: Initial Phase 2 pass, N-Series and F-Series only. H-Series absent (Phase 1 had not yet incorporated it). Several coverage gaps left undocumented as explicit unresolved_positions entries.

PHASE 2 CLOSURE PASS. H-Series position_universe added (block H-2005-2008, all three models). Cummins B6.7 F-Series gap explicitly documented. The two anomalous lube OEN rows cross-checked against a second extraction algorithm and against the adjacent RADIATOR block, ruling out an extraction error. Coverage closure means every Phase 1 vehicle x position cell now carries a terminal Phase 2 state (VERIFIED, NOT_APPLICABLE, or an honestly-documented PARTIAL/UNRESOLVED/CONFLICTING) -- it does NOT mean every cell is VERIFIED. See docs/hermes/ISUZU_US_DIESEL_CLOSURE_2000_2026.md, section 'PHASE 2 -- OFFICIALLY CLOSED', for the full coverage matrix and counts.

governance.scope_rule: Every isuzu_oe_oen row below reproduces the YEAR and ENGINE columns exactly as Isuzu published them. A row is only bound to a Phase 1 vehicle where that vehicle's own model year and engine both fall inside the published scope. Where Isuzu published an engine-scoped range but no model, the binding is recorded as ENGINE_SCOPED and the vehicle-level answer stays PARTIAL.
governance.model_line_rule: Isuzu heads its parts sections with model LINES: "N-SERIES NPR / NRR / NQR" and "F-SERIES FTR / FVR / FSR". A suffix variant of a named line is covered by that line - NPR-HD and NPR-XD by NPR, NRR DERATE by NRR, FVR DERATE by FVR. A model line Isuzu does not name is NOT covered, which is why FRR and FXR carry no filter row even though they share a block and an engine with FTR and FVR.
governance.h_series_rule: PHASE 2 PASS 2026-09-23. No Isuzu document anywhere in this closure publishes a model-line grouping for H-Series comparable to "N-SERIES NPR / NRR / NQR" -- Isuzu's own H-Series specification pages list HTR, HVR and HXR as three separate models, each with its own dedicated specification page and its own GVWR, horsepower and torque range, with no shared parts table. HTR, HVR and HXR are therefore each fully independent for filter-position purposes: none may inherit from either of the other two, and none may inherit from F-Series merely because both share the 6HK1-TC engine family. This is the same model-line rule applied more strictly, because H-Series publishes no grouped parts table at all to even test for a shared line.
governance.cummins_b67_rule: PHASE 2 PASS 2026-09-23. MY2022-2026 F-Series uses the Cummins B6.7, confirmed by Isuzu's own brochures in Phase 1 (ISUZU_FTR_SPECS_BROCHURE_2022, ISUZU_2025_F_BROCHURE). No Isuzu-published filter part number for this engine was located in this pass. Per the task's explicit instruction, Cummins official parts/maintenance literature may be used as OEM engine evidence only where Isuzu does not publish its own number AND the exact Isuzu chassis application is established; Fleetguard is explicitly excluded from Phase 2 authority even though Cummins-owned, and belongs to Phase 3. No Cummins document meeting that bar was located in this pass either (see unresolved_positions), so this remains UNRESOLVED rather than filled from a Fleetguard or other aftermarket source.
governance.retailer_leads_not_evidence: Several retailer/marketplace listings (eBay, Amazon, Walmart, and similar cross-reference sites) were encountered while researching the gaps below and are recorded in unresolved_positions purely as research leads for a future, governance-approved primary-source confirmation pass. None of them defines fitment or evidence_status in this file, per the task's explicit prohibition on retailers/forums as defining evidence.

position_universe.derivation: Taken from the Isuzu maintenance schedules in the 2006 and 2007 NPR diesel owner's manuals and from the F-Series Priority Service Maintenance Program text, not assumed from the manifest's position list.

AIR_SECONDARY.basis: No secondary or safety air element appears anywhere in the 2006 or 2007 NPR maintenance schedules or in the N-Series section of the Isuzu parts cross reference.

LUBE_SECONDARY.basis: Only one engine oil filter appears in the maintenance schedule.

FUEL_PRIMARY.service: replace the fuel filter and drain water from the water separator every 15,000 miles (24,000 km)

FUEL_SECONDARY.basis: The N-Series maintenance schedule lists a single combined 'Fuel Filter / Water Separator' item, but the Isuzu parts cross reference lists several distinct diesel fuel filter part numbers for overlapping years. Whether those are alternates, a primary/secondary pair or successive revisions is not settled by the sources retrieved.

FUEL_WATER_SEPARATOR.note: Combined with FUEL_PRIMARY in the schedule. A separately numbered high-efficiency fuel/water separator appears in the parts cross reference only from the 2022i range.

CABIN.status_note: Isuzu specifies cleaning, not replacement, and publishes no cabin filter part number in the retrieved sources. It is therefore an applicable position with an UNRESOLVED part number, not a NOT_APPLICABLE one.

AIR_DRYER.basis: N-Series service brakes are vacuum/hydraulic or hydraulic-boosted with 4-channel ABS throughout 2000-2026. There is no air brake system and therefore no air dryer.

TRANSMISSION_FILTER.service: replace fluid and external filter every 30,000 miles (48,000 km), or every 24 months

HYDRAULIC_FILTER.basis: No hydraulic filter appears in the Isuzu chassis maintenance schedule. Body-builder hydraulics are outside the Isuzu-published chassis maintenance scope.

DPF.service: clean every 100,000 miles (160,000 km) or every 3,000 hours
DPF.status_note: An emissions aftertreatment device that Isuzu schedules for cleaning, not a maintenance filter in the ELIMFILTERS sense. Recorded for completeness and excluded from the filter-set answer.

AIR_PRIMARY.basis: No F-Series air filter row exists in the Isuzu parts cross reference, and no F-Series owner's manual was retrieved.

AIR_SECONDARY.basis: Heavy-duty air cleaners on this class commonly carry a safety element, but no Isuzu USA document retrieved states one for the F-Series.

FUEL_PRIMARY.isuzu_part_description: FUEL FILTER / ELEMENT KIT; FUEL FILTER

FUEL_SECONDARY.basis: The Isuzu F-Series Priority Service Maintenance Program text states the plan covers 'replacing engine and chassis fuel filters' - two distinct serviced fuel filter positions.

FUEL_WATER_SEPARATOR.basis: No separately numbered F-Series fuel/water separator appears in the Isuzu parts cross reference.

CABIN.basis: No F-Series owner's manual or cabin filter part number was retrieved.

AIR_DRYER.basis: Isuzu publishes air brakes on the F-Series across the whole period - 'Rear air brake' and 'Parking Air Brake' in the 2016 FTR brochure and 'Full Air Dual Circuit with ABS' on the current FTR. An air-braked chassis carries an air dryer, but no Isuzu air dryer cartridge part number was retrieved.

TRANSMISSION_FILTER.basis: F-Series transmissions across the period are Isuzu manual, Allison AT545, Allison 1000/2000 and Allison 2550 RDS. No Isuzu-published F-Series transmission filter part number was retrieved.

HYDRAULIC_FILTER.basis: Not part of the Isuzu-published chassis maintenance scope.

H-SERIES.derivation_note: PHASE 2 PASS 2026-09-23. Derived from the Isuzu H-Series microsite (isuzucv.com/hseries/*) already read in the Phase 1 closure -- specifically the model-specific specification pages (htrspecs.html, hvrspecs.html, hxrspecs.html), which give transmission and brake-system configuration but were never accompanied by an owner's manual, service manual or parts catalogue in any Wayback capture found. No maintenance-schedule document exists for this series in the sources retrieved, so every position below rests on inference from the vehicle's own published configuration (what kind of engine, brakes, transmission it has) rather than on an explicit Isuzu maintenance-schedule line item the way N-Series and F-Series do.

AIR_PRIMARY.basis: The 6HK1-TC is an air-breathing diesel and therefore requires an intake air filter as a matter of engineering necessity, but no Isuzu H-Series document of any kind (specification page, brochure, manual) publishes a part number or even confirms a single- vs two-stage air cleaner.

AIR_SECONDARY.basis: Not stated by Isuzu for H-Series. The contemporaneous F-Series shares the 6HK1-TC and is itself UNRESOLVED for this position, so there is no in-scope Isuzu evidence to reason from either way.

LUBE_PRIMARY.basis: No Isuzu H-Series document publishes an oil filter part number.

LUBE_SECONDARY.basis: Not stated by Isuzu for H-Series.

FUEL_PRIMARY.basis: No Isuzu H-Series document publishes a fuel filter part number.

FUEL_SECONDARY.basis: Not stated by Isuzu for H-Series.

FUEL_WATER_SEPARATOR.basis: Not stated by Isuzu for H-Series.

CABIN.basis: No Isuzu H-Series owner's manual or cabin filter part number was retrieved.

AIR_DRYER.basis: Isuzu's own model-specific specification pages (captured 2005-03-18, re-checked unchanged through 2009-06-16) publish brake system as a per-model configuration, not a uniform H-Series attribute: HTR -- Standard 'Hydraulic 4-piston', Optional 'ABS Full Air'; HVR -- Standard 'Hydraulic 4-piston', Optional 'Air brake'; HXR -- Standard 'Air brake', Optional 'Air brake'. An air dryer is only present on a vehicle actually built with the (standard-on-HXR, optional-on-HTR/HVR) full-air brake system. No Isuzu document states which configuration any given VIN or fleet order actually received, and no air dryer cartridge part number was published for any configuration.

HTR.air_dryer_applicability: CONDITIONAL -- only if the optional full-air brake system was ordered

HVR.air_dryer_applicability: CONDITIONAL -- only if the optional full-air brake system was ordered

HXR.air_dryer_applicability: APPLICABLE as standard -- HXR ships with air brakes; part number still UNRESOLVED

TRANSMISSION_FILTER.basis: Isuzu's H-Series specification pages list transmission options as Allison 2400/2500 HS/RDS automatic (HTR/HVR), Allison 3000/3500 RDS automatic (HVR/HXR), or Eaton Fuller manual (all three). A serviceable external filter would apply only to the Allison automatic configuration, and Isuzu does not state which transmission any given vehicle carries or publish a filter part number for either.

HYDRAULIC_FILTER.basis: Not part of the Isuzu-published chassis maintenance scope, consistent with N-Series and F-Series.

unresolved_positions.phase2_pass_2026-09-23_note: A targeted search for Cummins-official B6.7 filter part numbers tied explicitly to the Isuzu F-Series chassis application (the standard this closure's own rules require before Cummins literature may serve as OEM evidence) did not locate a qualifying document. General Cummins B6.7 filter listings exist (e.g. Cummins Fuel Filter 3975126 on shop.cummins.com) but none found establishes the Isuzu-chassis linkage; using them without that linkage would violate the same no-inheritance principle applied everywhere else in this closure. Remains UNRESOLVED. Aftermarket B6.7 references (Fleetguard/Donaldson) were seen during this search and are explicitly excluded from Phase 2 per governance.cummins_b67_rule; they belong to Phase 3.

unresolved_positions.scope: H-SERIES all models (HTR, HVR, HXR), MY2005-2008, all positions
unresolved_positions.reason: PHASE 2 PASS 2026-09-23. H-Series is newly incorporated into Phase 1 and had zero Phase 2 coverage before this pass. An exhaustive search (isuzucv.com's full archived history for any H-Series manual/parts/service page, general web search for HTR/HVR/HXR filter part numbers) found the model-specific specification pages already used in Phase 1 (engine, GVWR, transmission, brake configuration) but no owner's manual, service manual or parts catalogue of any kind for this product line was ever archived or found. Retailer listings (research leads only, not evidence) associate the F-Series/H-Series-shared lube filter number 1132004872 with HTR specifically by engine family (6HK1), which is a plausible but explicitly-prohibited model-to-model inheritance pattern under this closure's own rules (H-Series may not inherit from F-Series merely because both use 6HK1-TC) -- it is recorded here as a lead, not applied.
unresolved_positions.closing_note: Every H-Series position nonetheless has a terminal state per position_universe.H-SERIES: HYDRAULIC_FILTER is NOT_APPLICABLE (consistent with N/F-Series); AIR_DRYER is the one position with a documented, per-model CONDITIONAL basis (see position_universe.H-SERIES.AIR_DRYER.by_model) even though its part number is UNRESOLVED; every other position is UNRESOLVED with its own stated basis. No H-Series position was silently omitted from the coverage matrix.
